hard_rules: Do not use RGB or embedded global_id as tracking input.
Rolling observation mismatch is not axial rigid rotation.
Rolling mismatch does not create a large contiguous hole.
Partial occlusion is side-based; center band is preserved.
Yaw is an explicit Z-axis rotation and is independent of rolling observation mismatch.
Layer-1 has at most 10 slots and can contain two edge-grown clusters separated by a normal large free region.
OCCLUDED requires a positive current instance; zero-point historical observations are abnormal and are not normal occlusion.
TOP_DOWN_Z is generated with a global XY z-buffer for rays along world -Z; it is not a naive z>center crop.
Identity and motion anomaly are separate: semantic-unique identity may remain MATCHED inside the hard X envelope while motion is marked ABNORMAL.
Second-layer loading is legal only after layer-1 is full with 10 coils.
When second-layer loading is active, layer-1 is a locked support foundation; significant layer-1 motion is an abnormal/collapse-risk condition.
Second-layer semantic slot k is the support valley between layer-1 slots k and k+1.
Double-layer bootstrap requires positive current point evidence for every layer-1 coil; severe partial visibility is allowed, zero-point inferred coils are not committed.

topdown_view.note: Synthetic Z sequences preserve at least a small top-facing observation for every historical coil per current operating assumption.

motion_envelope.inside_hard_policy: semantic-unique identity may be MATCHED with ABNORMAL_X_MOTION; beyond hard => UNCERTAIN

double_layer.upper_slot_definition: slot k is supported by layer1 slots k and k+1
double_layer.foundation_motion_interpretation: Locked L1: translation is collapse-risk evidence; top-down partial-view centroid/yaw bias is not treated as physical movement unless it breaches top-down displacement envelopes.
